observations: The independent original-pixel inventory was written before reading the retained inventory or opening the current candidate. One continuous schematic, one AC generator, one step-up and three step-down rectangles are present in both original and current output.

All 13 paired runs are retained: one generator input connection, three inter-transformer connections, six open upper/lower diagonal branches, and three distinct final horizontal user outputs. Each run has two strokes, not an invented extra branch or phase-count claim.

The source numerical multiplicities are exactly preserved: one 11 kV, one 110 kV, three 35 kV, three 6 kV, and four 220 V annotations. Splitting a number and its unit onto two lines does not add or change a value.

Generator and 11 kV remain on the input side of the step-up transformer. 110 kV remains between step-up and first step-down; 35 kV remains between the first and second step-down; 6 kV remains between the second and third step-down.

Each 35 kV, 6 kV and 220 V upper/lower diagonal label stays with the corresponding transformer's outgoing pair. In particular, all three bottom voltage labels and both final diagonal pairs are present, not clipped or transferred to another stage.

All three final horizontal pairs leave the final transformer and share the Users group label. The two source horizontal 220 V inscriptions remain in the two inter-pair spaces; the candidate neither inserts a fifth 220 V inscription nor removes the upper horizontal pair.

The retained 20 inventory groups map to actual visible objects and their stated assertions. The independent count and semantic comparison, rather than that stored mapping or the 65-object native count, establish source completeness.
No grid, axis, named point, current value, load-specific symbol, direction arrowhead or converter is present in the source, and none is invented in the candidate.

observations: The AC wave inside the generator and the transformer-only apparatus identify this as the staged AC transmission/distribution schematic described immediately before Figure 63 in the unchanged approved N35 text; it is not incorrectly presented as the later HVDC converter arrangement.

The first device correctly raises 11 kV to 110 kV. Subsequent devices correctly lower 110 kV to 35 kV, 35 kV to 6 kV, and 6 kV to 220 V. The final comparison respects units: 6 kV is 6000 V, greater than 220 V.
The upper, lower and continuing branches at the 35 kV and 6 kV stages all carry their own output-stage voltage; none is labelled with its incoming higher voltage.

The final outgoing diagonal and horizontal supply group is associated with the final low-voltage transformer, not the preceding 6 kV transmission segment. The schematic does not claim a different voltage for an unannotated output.

The visible branching serves the approved explanation of staged reduction and delivery to distributed users. No current arrows, equal branch loads, escalating current values, universal voltage standard, lossless real transformer, or guaranteed power claim is added.

The prose's separate 500 kV and 16-20 kV examples are not substituted for this source schematic's 110 kV and 11 kV labels. They describe examples, not a contradictory requirement to renumber Figure 63.

Each semantic conductor has retained connects and parallel assertions; generator terminals also have pointOnCircle assertions, and transformer labels have inside assertions. Existing native validation is corroboration only and was not rerun.
This is an explanatory figure, not an exercise solution: no answer key, calculation, standard answer or new question is exposed or authored.
